The paragraph describes a scenario involving a retail store, 'Best Deals', extending working hours during the holiday season. To assess compliance with legal standards, we must look at the specific actions and constraints mentioned.

First, the text states that employees were "already working the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws." This implies that any further extension of hours would likely violate those local labor laws, as exceeding the maximum permitted hours is generally illegal.

Second, the store decided to "extend its working hours without increasing pay." In many jurisdictions, working beyond standard hours or on holidays may require overtime pay or premium pay rates. Paying the same rate for hours that legally require overtime compensation would constitute a violation of wage and hour laws.

Third, management claimed this was a "one-time exception." Legal compliance is not determined by the frequency of the violation or the intent to make it a one-time event. If the action violates the law, it remains non-compliant regardless of whether it is repeated.

Therefore, the actions described—extending hours beyond the legal maximum and failing to provide increased pay for those hours—are non-compliant with standard legal labor standards. The scenario depicts illegal labor practices.
